The bug has been fixed and verified.

### Root Cause
In [`BaseSecantSolver.java`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/math_50_group_d_fix/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/math/analysis/solvers/BaseSecantSolver.java#L185-L191), the `case REGULA_FALSI` block contained an artificial interval adjustment (`if (x == x1) { ... }`) that modified `x0` and evaluated the objective value. This deviated from the standard *Regula Falsi* (false position) algorithm where `f0` and `x0` remain unchanged when the interval is not inverted. Because of this artificial progression, the solver converged prematurely rather than exhibiting the expected slow convergence and throwing a `TooManyEvaluationsException` when exceeding the evaluation limit.

### Fix
Removed the artificial interval update logic under `case REGULA_FALSI` in [`BaseSecantSolver.java`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/math_50_group_d_fix/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/math/analysis/solvers/BaseSecantSolver.java#L185-L188) so that standard *Regula Falsi* behavior is restored.

### Verification
- Ran the BDD verification test: `export TZ='America/Los_Angeles'; mvn test -Dtest=CucumberTest` (passed).
- Generated the patch file with only the source modifications saved to [`enlightened_fix.patch`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/math_50_group_d_fix/enlightened_fix.patch).
